claims.text: The initial equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi alloy is a single-phase FCC high-entropy alloy.
The initial alloy has equiaxed grains approximately 50 µm in size.
The initial alloy contains less than 100 ppm bulk dissolved oxygen.
Elevated-temperature exposure in residual oxygen causes oxygen to segregate to CoCrFeMnNi grain boundaries.
Grain-boundary oxygen segregation reduces grain-boundary cohesive strength.
Reduced grain-boundary cohesion shifts fracture from transgranular ductile tearing to intergranular brittle cracking.
Oxygen-induced intergranular cracking causes a marked loss of fracture toughness relative to inert-aged material.
Clean grain boundaries in conventional alloys remain ductile under similar aging conditions.
Aging in 10^-3 atm O2 at 600 °C for 500 h will produce greater grain-boundary oxygen enrichment than identical aging in high-purity Ar containing less than 1 ppm O2.
O2-aged specimens will exhibit an approximately 30–50% reduction in K_IC relative to the as-annealed baseline.
O2-aged specimens will exhibit an approximately 30–50% reduction in K_IC relative to Ar-aged specimens.
Ar-aged specimens will retain fracture toughness within ±5% of the as-annealed baseline.
The as-annealed CoCrFeMnNi alloy has K_IC of approximately 200 MPa√m.
The proposed embrittlement mechanism applies to thermal exposures from 400 to 800 °C for up to 1000 h.
The proposed embrittlement mechanism applies at quasi-static strain rates below 10^-2 s^-1.
The proposed embrittlement mechanism applies at test temperatures from 77 K to 300 K.
